title: Turn your coding agent's mistakes into tests and checks
summary: A developer had Claude Code review a session that shipped a numbering bug with 42 green tests; its fixes became a test and commit check, and a fresh run passed 5/5.
agent_role: Claude Code built the feature, then reviewed its own session log to propose fixes once told about the failure; the human approved which fixes to keep.
outcome: Author reports the re-run in a fresh session passed the hidden finance check five out of five times.
what_they_did: A developer asked Claude Code to add numbered credit notes to a small invoicing app. Tests passed, but a hidden check found a rejected request wasted a number. They ran a review skill on the session, told it what failed, and made it quote the moment behind each suggestion. Approved fixes became a test, a check that runs before every save to the code history, a coding rule and a code comment.
how_it_went: The first review called the session smooth and missed the bug. After being told the failure, it found the cause and kept four of five suggestions. A fresh session read the new rule and test and passed the check 5/5.
worth_knowing: The review cannot see failures the session never saw, so tell it what broke. Only the pre-commit check is enforced; written rules work only if the agent chooses to read them.
prompt: Review this coding session's log. Here is what failed after you finished: [describe the bug]. Find the moment in the session that caused it and quote it. List what would have prevented it, ranked, and drop any idea you cannot tie to a specific moment. For each survivor, suggest the right place for it: a test, a check that runs before commits, a line in [coding standards file], or a code comment. Do not edit any files; show me the list and wait for my approval.

curation.rationale: Detailed, honest experiment showing how a coding agent's retrospective turned a hidden bug into a test, a pre-commit check and a coding rule, with a passing re-run; specific and reproducible.
